proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-accessible-system-ranks] to the small family of categories under consideration and to $F,G$ when present, taking the bound $b\geq |S|$. Write its two cardinals as $\lambda<\kappa$. Thus all required categories are $\kappa$-accessible, $F,G$ preserve $\kappa$-filtered colimits, $F$ takes $\kappa$-presentables to $\kappa$-presentables, and the categories and functors admit/preserve $\lambda$-indexed chain colimits: the regular ordinal $\lambda$ is $\lambda$-filtered. These are separate choices for each application of (1), (2), or (3). In particular $|S|<\kappa$.

source.place: Paragraph 2 auxiliary cardinal choice; Positselski, hypotheses preceding Theorems 3.1 and 4.1 Agent-written expansion; online comparison: https://cahierstgdc.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/10/Positetski-LXV-4.pdf.

proof.text: Two presentability facts will be used. A colimit of a diagram of $\kappa$-presentable objects with fewer than $\kappa$ arrows, whenever that colimit exists, is $\kappa$-presentable by [lem-coef-ordinary-small-colimit-presentable] (its Hom functor is the limit of their Hom functors over the opposite index category). The remaining consequences come from [lem-coef-accessible-set-functor-limits]. Products of fewer than $\kappa$ functors preserving $\kappa$-filtered colimits and equalizers of such functors also preserve these colimits, by its discrete and parallel-pair cases. For use in the constructions below, presentability gives factorization of a map into a $\kappa$-filtered colimit at a stage and equality of two such maps after a later stage: the Hom comparison is a bijection, and a filtered colimit of sets is represented by elements at stages, with equality witnessed at a common later stage (refine the finite zigzag in the disjoint-union quotient to one cocone). Fewer than $\kappa$ such requirements can be imposed at once by a cocone on their witnessing objects and arrows.

source.place: Paragraph 2 auxiliary Hom calculation; Positselski, Proposition 2.1 and proofs of Propositions 3.2, 4.2, 4.3 Agent-written expansion; online comparison: https://cahierstgdc.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/10/Positetski-LXV-4.pdf.

proof.text: Use [lem-coef-accessible-presentable-density] for each $\kappa$-accessible ambient category. We may replace all $\kappa$-presentables by a small representative family: for an initial small generating family, the identity of a $\kappa$-presentable object factors through one term of its filtered presentation, making it a retract of a generator. A splitting of an idempotent on a fixed generator is unique up to isomorphism (the two comparison maps are the retraction followed by the other section, and their composites are identities). There are only a small set of these idempotents, since Hom sets are small. Consequently all $\kappa$-presentables have a small representative family. Restricting the canonical diagram to those representatives preserves both its cocones and filteredness, by transporting objects and arrows through their chosen isomorphisms. Denote the resulting small, $\kappa$-filtered, colimiting presentation of $X$ by $D_X=\mathcal A_\kappa/X$.

source.place: Paragraph 2 auxiliary smallness of presentations; Positselski, section 1 and Lemma 1.1 Agent-written expansion; online comparison: https://cahierstgdc.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/10/Positetski-LXV-4.pdf.

proof.text: For (1), form products and cocones coordinatewise. The universal property [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] shows that a coordinatewise colimit is a colimit of tuples, so the product has $\kappa$-filtered colimits and its projections preserve them. A tuple $(P_s)$ of $\kappa$-presentables is $\kappa$-presentable because its Hom functor is the product of the coordinate Hom functors, and $|S|<\kappa$; apply [lem-coef-accessible-set-functor-limits]. Given $X=(X_s)$, present each $X_s$ by its small canonical diagram from [lem-coef-accessible-presentable-density] and step 3. The product of these index categories is small and $\kappa$-filtered: for a diagram with fewer than $\kappa$ arrows choose its cone in each coordinate. Its tuple diagram has colimit $X$: projection to any one index is final directly, since all other index categories are nonempty and filtered, so a compatible cocone in that coordinate is precisely a cocone on the original coordinate diagram. Thus the small product of the small families of presentables generates. If $S$ is empty, the terminal category is generated by its unique object. If a factor is empty, the product is empty and accessibility is vacuous, with empty generating family.

source.place: Paragraph 2 product closure; Positselski, Proposition 2.1 Agent-written expansion; online comparison: https://cahierstgdc.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/10/Positetski-LXV-4.pdf.

proof.text: For (2), let $E=\operatorname{Ins}(F,G)$ and $U:E\to\mathcal A$. If $(X_i,u_i)$ is a small $\kappa$-filtered diagram and $X=\operatorname{colim}X_i$, define $u:FX\to GX$ by the compatible maps $FX_i\xrightarrow{u_i}GX_i\to GX$, using preservation by $F$. For a cocone into $(Y,v)$ its unique underlying map $h:X\to Y$ satisfies $G(h)u=vF(h)$ after precomposition with each $FX_i\to FX$, hence it satisfies the equation. This proves that $U$ creates these colimits. For a $\lambda$-chain, its underlying colimit exists and $F$ preserves it by step 1; define $u$ using its chain legs, and check $G(h)u=vF(h)$ on those same legs. Thus $U$ also creates the chain colimit. The Hom set from $(P,w)$ is the equalizer of $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal A}(P,-)$ and the two maps into $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal B}(FP,G(-))$ given by $h\mapsto G(h)w$ and $h\mapsto uF(h)$. When $P$ is $\kappa$-presentable, so is $FP$ by step 1. Both set-valued functors preserve $\kappa$-filtered colimits, using preservation by $G$. By [lem-coef-accessible-set-functor-limits], $(P,w)$ is $\kappa$-presentable in $E$.

source.place: Paragraph 2 inserter colimits and Hom equalizer; Positselski, Proposition 4.2 Agent-written expansion; online comparison: https://cahierstgdc.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/10/Positetski-LXV-4.pdf.

proof.text:
Fix $(X,u)\in E$. Here is the extension construction that supplies generators and their relations. Let $T\to X$ have $T$ $\kappa$-presentable. Specify fewer than $\kappa$ objects $(P_a,w_a)\to(X,u)$ with $P_a$ $\kappa$-presentable and maps $h_a:P_a\to T$ over $X$. Begin at $T_0=T$ in the canonical filtered presentation $D_X$ of step 3. Construct objects $t_i:T_i\to X$ and compatible transition maps $a_{ij}:T_i\to T_j$, $i<j<\lambda$, together with $v_i:FT_i\to GT_{i+1}$ satisfying $G(t_{i+1})v_i=uF(t_i)$ and
$$G(a_{j+1,i+1})v_j=v_iF(a_{ji})\quad(j<i).$$
At the first successor require also $v_0F(h_a)=G(a_{01}h_a)w_a$ for every $a$. For any successor $i+1$, factor $uF(t_i)$ through some $GT'$ because $FT_i$ is $\kappa$-presentable and $GX=\operatorname{colim}_{D_X}GT'$. Take a common upper cone with $T_i$ in $D_X$. All the required equations hold after mapping to $GX$; their domains are $FT_j$, and initially $FP_a$, which are $\kappa$-presentable. The eventual-equality argument of step 2 and $\kappa$-filteredness let us enlarge this stage so that all equations hold simultaneously; there are fewer than $\kappa$ of them. At a limit $i<\lambda$ take a cocone in $D_X$ on all preceding stages and transitions, a diagram with fewer than $\kappa$ arrows, and then perform the same successor construction. This defines the chain without assuming that its proper initial segments have colimits in $\mathcal A$.

source.place: Paragraph 2 inserter extension construction; Positselski, Lemma 4.5 and proof of Proposition 4.3 Agent-written expansion; online comparison: https://cahierstgdc.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/10/Positetski-LXV-4.pdf.

proof.text: Take $Q=\operatorname{colim}_{i<\lambda}T_i$, which exists by step 1. It is $\kappa$-presentable by step 2, since $\lambda<\kappa$. As $F$ preserves this chain colimit, the compatible maps $FT_i\xrightarrow{v_i}GT_{i+1}\to GQ$ define $w:FQ\to GQ$. The equations in step 6 give $G(q)w=uF(q)$ for $q:Q\to X$ and $wF(P_a\to Q)=G(P_a\to Q)w_a$. Hence $(Q,w)\to(X,u)$ is an inserter morphism, and every $h_a$ extends to an inserter morphism $(P_a,w_a)\to(Q,w)$. This extension also retains all equalities between the underlying maps into $T$, because each is postcomposed with the same $T\to Q$. With the family empty it factors any $\kappa$-presentable $T\to X$ through a small-underlying-object of $E$.

source.place: Paragraph 2 end of inserter extension; Positselski, end of Lemma 4.5 Agent-written expansion; online comparison: https://cahierstgdc.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/10/Positetski-LXV-4.pdf.

proof.text: Let $\Delta$ be the small category of arrows $(P,w)\to(X,u)$ with $P$ in the small representative family from step 3; it is small because the possible structures and arrows are small Hom sets. Given a diagram in $\Delta$ with fewer than $\kappa$ morphisms, take a cone on its underlying diagram in $D_X$ by [lem-coef-accessible-presentable-density], with apex $T\to X$. Apply steps 6-7 to all its objects and cone maps $P_a\to T$. The resulting $(Q,w)$ is $\kappa$-presentable but may not be the selected representative; choose a representative $Q'$ and an isomorphism $e:Q'\to Q$. Set $q'=qe$ and $w'=G(e^{-1})wF(e)$, and replace each cone leg $j_a:P_a\to Q$ by $e^{-1}j_a$. Then $G(q')w'=uF(q')$ and $G(e^{-1}j_a)w_a=w' F(e^{-1}j_a)$ by cancellation of $F(e)F(e^{-1})$ and $G(e^{-1})G(e)$. Composition with the common $e^{-1}$ preserves the cone equations, giving an apex $(Q',w')$ in $\Delta$. This includes the empty diagram, proving nonemptiness. Thus $\Delta$ is $\kappa$-filtered.

source.place: Paragraph 2 filteredness of structured presentations; Positselski, Proposition 4.3 Agent-written expansion; online comparison: https://cahierstgdc.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/10/Positetski-LXV-4.pdf.

proof.text: The underlying diagram of $\Delta$ has colimit $X$. To verify this directly, every object $P\to X$ of $D_X$ maps to an underlying object of $\Delta$ by the empty-family extension in step 7, followed by transport to the selected representative. Any two such choices can be joined compatibly with $P$: first use step 8 to map their structured targets to one structured target $W$; then use the filteredness of $D_X$ to equalize the two underlying arrows $P\rightrightarrows W$ after $W\to T$; finally apply steps 6-7 with the one prescribed structured object $W$ and map $W\to T$, and transport the resulting structured object to a representative. The resulting structured target still equalizes them. Therefore a cocone from the underlying $\Delta$-diagram to any $Z$ determines a map $P\to Z$ for each $P\to X$ by choosing a structured extension; these maps are independent of the choice by the preceding joining argument. For an arrow $P\to P'$ over $X$, choose an extension of $P'$; its precomposition is an extension of $P$, so these maps form a cocone on $D_X$. By [lem-coef-accessible-presentable-density] it extends uniquely to $X\to Z$, which is the required colimit universal property. Since $U$ creates $\kappa$-filtered colimits by step 5, $(X,u)$ is the colimit of its $\Delta$-diagram in $E$. There is a small family of all structures on representatives $P$, and these objects are $\kappa$-presentable by step 5. This proves accessibility of the inserter and of its projection.

source.place: Paragraph 2 density of structured presentations; Positselski, Proposition 4.4 and conclusion of Theorem 4.1 Agent-written expansion; online comparison: https://cahierstgdc.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/10/Positetski-LXV-4.pdf.

proof.text: For (3), let $E$ be the equifier. Given a $\kappa$-filtered diagram in $E$ with colimit $X$ in $\mathcal A$, naturality and preservation by $F$ show $\alpha_X=\beta_X$: their composites with every $FX_i\to FX$ agree. Since $E$ is full, the same cocone is a colimit in $E$. Thus its inclusion creates $\kappa$-filtered colimits. For a $\lambda$-chain in $E$, step 1 supplies its colimit $X$ and preservation by $F$. Naturality makes the composites of $\alpha_X$ and $\beta_X$ with each chain leg $FX_i\to FX$ equal; the colimit universal property gives $\alpha_X=\beta_X$, and fullness makes this a colimit in $E$. The Hom functor of an object $P\in E$ is the restriction of $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal A}(P,-)$, so if $P$ is $\kappa$-presentable in $\mathcal A$, it is $\kappa$-presentable in $E$.

source.place: Paragraph 2 equifier colimits and presentability; Positselski, beginning of proof of Theorem 3.1 Agent-written expansion; online comparison: https://cahierstgdc.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/10/Positetski-LXV-4.pdf.

proof.text:
Let $X\in E$ and let $P\to X$ have $P$ $\kappa$-presentable in $\mathcal A$. Starting at $T_0=P$ in $D_X$, construct a $\lambda$-chain of $\kappa$-presentables $t_i:T_i\to X$ with transitions $a_{ij}$, requiring
$$G(a_{i,i+1})\alpha_{T_i}=G(a_{i,i+1})\beta_{T_i}.$$
The two maps agree after composition to $GX$, since $\alpha_X=\beta_X$ and naturality holds. Since $FT_i$ is $\kappa$-presentable and $GX=\operatorname{colim}_{D_X}GT$, eventual equality from step 2 gives a successor stage satisfying this equation. At a limit $i<\lambda$, choose a compatible upper cone in $D_X$, using its $\kappa$-filteredness, and continue. Set $Q=\operatorname{colim}_{i<\lambda}T_i$; this exists by step 1 and is $\kappa$-presentable by step 2. Since $FQ=\operatorname{colim}_{i<\lambda}FT_i$, the displayed equations and naturality give $\alpha_Q=\beta_Q$. Hence $P\to X$ factors through $Q\in E$ that is $\kappa$-presentable in $\mathcal A$.

source.place: Paragraph 2 equifier approximation; Positselski, Proposition 3.2 Agent-written expansion; online comparison: https://cahierstgdc.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/10/Positetski-LXV-4.pdf.

proof.text: Take the small representative family of step 3 and retain its members in $E$. For an isomorphism $e:Q\xrightarrow{\sim}R$ with $Q\in E$, naturality gives $\alpha_R=G(e)\alpha_QF(e^{-1})=G(e)\beta_QF(e^{-1})=\beta_R$, so its selected representative $R$ also belongs to $E$. For each $X\in E$, let $\Delta_E/X$ be the full subcategory of the small canonical category $D_X$ on arrows whose sources belong to this retained family. Step 11 followed by representative transport gives an arrow from every object $P\to X$ of $D_X$ to an object of $\Delta_E/X$. Explicitly, if $P\xrightarrow{h}Q\xrightarrow{q}X$ is the factorization in step 11 and $e:Q\xrightarrow{\sim}R$ is the representative isomorphism, use $eh:P\to R$ and $qe^{-1}:R\to X$.

source.place: Paragraph 2 equifier generation; Positselski, proof of Theorem 3.1 Agent-written expansion; online comparison: https://cahierstgdc.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/10/Positetski-LXV-4.pdf.

proof.text: The category $\Delta_E/X$ is $\kappa$-filtered. Indeed, regard a diagram in it with fewer than $\kappa$ arrows as a diagram in $D_X$. Canonical density [lem-coef-accessible-presentable-density], with the representatives of step 3, supplies a cocone with apex $T\to X$ in $D_X$. By step 12 choose an arrow from this apex to an object of $\Delta_E/X$ and postcompose every cocone leg with it. Fullness puts all these legs in $\Delta_E/X$, and associativity preserves their cocone equations. The same construction for the empty diagram supplies an object.

source.place: Paragraph 2 equifier generation; Positselski, proof of Theorem 3.1 Agent-written expansion; online comparison: https://cahierstgdc.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/10/Positetski-LXV-4.pdf.

proof.text: The underlying diagram of $\Delta_E/X$ has colimit $X$ in $\mathcal A$. Apply clause (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-colimit-initial-full-subcategory] with $\mathcal I=D_X^{\mathrm{op}}$, $\mathcal J=(\Delta_E/X)^{\mathrm{op}}$ and with the functor $\mathcal I^{\mathrm{op}}=D_X\to\mathcal A$ sending $(P,p)$ to $P$. The category $D_X$ is filtered by canonical density [lem-coef-accessible-presentable-density], so $\mathcal I$ is cofiltered. The subcategory is full, and step 12 gives exactly the required arrows $j\to i$ in the opposite category. Canonical density and step 3 give the ambient colimit $X$ with legs $p:P\to X$. The cited clause identifies the restricted colimit with this ambient one by the canonical comparison induced by those same legs. Hence the cocone on $\Delta_E/X$ with vertex $X$ and legs $p$ is colimiting, rather than merely having a vertex isomorphic to an unrelated colimit.

source.place: Tags 0BUC (lemma-cofinal-in-filtered) and 04E7 (lemma-cofinal), applied to the opposite of the small canonical presentation; same equifier-generation argument as the original step 12.

proof.text: For $Z\in E$, fullness identifies maps $X\to Z$ and all cocone equations with their counterparts in $\mathcal A$, so the unique factorization from step 14 is also the unique factorization in $E$; this is the colimit universal property [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. By step 13 its index is small and $\kappa$-filtered. Step 10 makes its sources $\kappa$-presentable in $E$ and gives all small $\kappa$-filtered colimits in $E$, preserved by inclusion. The retained small family therefore generates $E$, and both $E$ and its inclusion are accessible. If $E$ is empty there is no $X$ to consider and its empty family generates it. This proves (3); each of (1)-(3) has its own witnessing rank, as asserted.
